data.description:
## Context / Problem

Blocking links written before the structural resolver lands were resolved by ticket type tier, so the store already holds edges that are wrong under the new rule: epics blocked by their own children, and dependencies escalated to an ancestor that is not the nearest common ancestor's child. These do not self-heal — a `LINK` event is durable, and nothing re-resolves it on read — so `ready`, `next-batch` and the parent-first claim cascade stay distorted for as long as the edge exists. Bug 1803-df54-18bb-4881 records one instance already fixed by hand on epic 8fc2-0306-a9a0-4864 (children retyped to `story`, the spurious epic-to-child edge unlinked); the number of remaining instances is unknown because nothing can currently enumerate them.

## Approach

Add `rebar link-audit`, a store-wide scan over active blocking edges that reports two defect classes, plus an opt-in `--repair` that fixes them:

- **ancestor-blocking**: the edge's source is an ancestor or descendant of its target. Always wrong; repair unlinks it.
- **mis-escalated**: re-resolving the edge's endpoints through `resolve_hierarchy_link` [rebar:7ab3-9df0-7a90-4ffd] yields a different pair than the one on disk. Repair unlinks the recorded edge and writes the re-resolved one.

Repair reuses the existing `add_dependency` and `unlink` write paths rather than composing `LINK` / `UNLINK` events directly, so the cycle guards, closed-ticket guards and idempotency checks in `src/rebar/graph/_links.py` apply to repaired edges exactly as they do to new ones. It reports every rewrite it performs, because an edge already escalated under the old rule does not record the author's original endpoints and the re-resolution is therefore a best-effort reconstruction, not a provable restoration.

`--repair` is gated behind an explicit flag with `--dry-run` for preview, mirroring the flag conventions `fsck_cli` already establishes at `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:429`. Default invocation is read-only.

Rejected alternative: fold these checks into `rebar fsck` as a sixth check. `fsck` validates event and storage integrity — JSON validity, `CREATE` presence, `SNAPSHOT` consistency — whereas this validates dependency-graph semantics over a well-formed store; the two answer different questions and have different repair risk profiles. `src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py` is also 539 lines against the 800-line module cap, and its `--repair` cluster was already split out to `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py` for that reason, so adding a scan there works against the module-size policy.

Rejected alternative: repair automatically on read, re-resolving edges as the graph is loaded. That would make every read path depend on the resolver and would silently mutate the store during nominally read-only commands.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_commands/link_audit.py` — new module: the scan, the two defect classifiers, the repair driver, and `link_audit_cli` parsing `--repair`, `--dry-run` and `--output json`.
- `src/rebar/_commands/__init__.py` — register `link-audit` in `_ARGV_REGISTRY` (line 66), alongside the other variadic commands that parse their own argv.
- `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` — add `link-audit` to `_WRITES_FULL` (line 126) so `--repair` gets full auto-init and reconverge before writing.
- `src/rebar/_cli/help/link-audit.txt` — new help text, matching the format of `src/rebar/_cli/help/link.txt`.
- `docs/cli-reference.md` — document the command next to the existing `link` entry at line 236.
- `tests/scripts/graph/test_link_audit.py` — new test module.

## Testing

- Happy path: a store whose blocking edges are all valid under the structural rule reports zero findings and exits 0.
- Happy path: `--repair` on a store containing one ancestor-blocking edge removes it, and a second scan reports zero findings.
- Edge: a mis-escalated edge (recorded pair differs from the re-resolved pair) is reported as `mis-escalated`, and `--repair` replaces it with the re-resolved edge.
- Edge: the bug 1803 shape — an epic holding `depends_on` on its own child — is classified `ancestor-blocking` and removed by repair.
- Edge: a store with no blocking edges at all reports zero findings rather than erroring.
- Failure: `--repair` on an edge whose re-resolution would create a cycle reports the edge as unrepairable and leaves it in place, rather than raising out of the command.
- Failure: `--dry-run` with `--repair` writes no events; verified by asserting the event count is unchanged.
- Regression: non-blocking relations are never scanned, reported or rewritten.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar link-audit` with no flags writes no events; verified by comparing the tracker's event-file count before and after in `tests/scripts/graph/test_link_audit.py`.
- [ ] An epic holding `depends_on` on its own child is reported as `ancestor-blocking`, and `--repair` removes it so a second scan reports zero findings; verified by the repair case in `tests/scripts/graph/test_link_audit.py`.
- [ ] An edge whose re-resolution differs from the recorded pair is reported as `mis-escalated` and replaced by `--repair`; verified by the mis-escalation case in the same test module.
- [ ] `--repair --dry-run` leaves the event count unchanged while still reporting the findings it would fix; verified by the dry-run case in the same test module.
- [ ] `rebar link-audit --output json` emits a parseable object whose findings carry a `kind` of `ancestor-blocking` or `mis-escalated`; verified by parsing the output with `json.loads` in the test module.
- [ ] Running `rebar link-audit --repair` then `rebar link-audit` against this repository's own tracker yields an empty second report; verified by running both commands in the worktree and recording the output on this ticket.
- [ ] `pytest tests/scripts/graph/`, `make lint` and `make typecheck` all pass in the worktree; verified by running each.
- [ ] `src/rebar/_commands/link_audit.py` is between 100 and 800 lines, per the module-size policy; verified by `wc -l`.
data.title: rebar link-audit: detect and repair blocking edges written under the type-tier rule
